ios.desc:
ByePhotos helps you easily organize your phone media files and free up valuable storage space.

• Worry-free Security – Completely local processing, no internet connection required, ensuring your privacy
• Smart Recognition – Automatically detects similar/duplicate photos and recommends the best options to keep
• Video Compression – Reduce file sizes while preserving visual clarity, helping you save space without noticeably compromising quality
• Efficient Organization – Quick classification with gestures, one-click deletion of unwanted photos
• Easy Continuity – Multiple organization modes (Random, By Month, Oldest First, Newest First), real-time progress display, supports pause and resume anytime
• Full Format Support – Compatible with photos, videos, Live Photos

Organize a little bit every day, say goodbye to cluttered albums.
No need to complete all organization work at once. ByePhotos records your progress, allowing you to easily complete the task over multiple sessions, reducing organization stress.

Download ByePhotos and start cleaning up your iPhone photo library now. Rediscover precious memories while freeing up device storage space.
Making organization simple and memories more precious. ByePhotos, your photo organization assistant.


---

Subscription Information

Subscribe to ByePhotos annually or monthly. Members get access to all features with continuous updates.

Subscriptions automatically renew through iTunes. Your account will be charged 24 hours before expiration. To cancel, turn off auto-renewal in your iTunes/Apple ID settings at least 24 hours before the current period ends.

show_hn.title: Show HN: ByePhotos – An iOS App to Help you cleanup phone storage

quotes.text:
I developed an app to help clean up phone storage. Its main feature is to find similar photos in the photo album and provide a convenient interface for you to filter them. It also has a video compression feature that can significantly reduce the size of videos.

I know there are already many similar applications on the App Store, but there are always aspects of their design or interaction that I don't like, so I developed one myself. The process of thinking about app design and interaction made me feel that launching an app is quite interesting.

The app went live a few weeks ago, and for the first three days after the launch, I adopted a limited free strategy. On the first day, over 5,000 people claimed a lifetime license for free, and then I continuously received feedback from people who wanted to suggest improvements for the app. This process made me feel more connected with others.
